I'm not gonna' lie, its tough losing a dog you've had in your life for a long time. I just had my little chihuahua pass rather unexpectedly -- valley fever at the age of ten (average life span is years longer). I was by her side till the end, as she would've been for me.

I had her since she was the size of a pop can, eight weeks old. The first couple of months after her passing were rough. But things got better, and I still have all of the beautiful memories from those ten years. I find comfort in knowing we gave her a really good life; she was our world and we were her's. She became more than just an animal, and really was an unconditional companion.

So in retrospect, yes it was worth it. Do realize, though, a dog is more than just a possession. A dog needs love and attention, but will give back ten fold. The life-enrichment of such a relationship is beyond words. If I had the choice to make again, I would absolutely do the same.
